en.name: Eucharistic Miracle of Sokolka
en.summary: A host dropped during communion in 2008 developed a heart-tissue-like discoloration later studied by independent pathologists.
en.body: In October 2008, a consecrated host was accidentally dropped during the distribution of communion at a parish in Sokolka, Poland, and, following standard practice, was placed in water inside the tabernacle safe to dissolve. A week later, a nun preparing to dispose of the water noticed a red spot had formed on the host resembling a clot of blood. The relic was dried and preserved, and years later independent medical experts, given samples without being told their origin, examined the tissue and reported it closely resembled heart muscle in a state consistent with a person in agony, findings that could not be explained by ordinary contamination. The Archbishop of Bialystok recognized the event as worthy of belief, and the relic is now enshrined in a side chapel of the Sokolka parish church, drawing pilgrims from across Poland.
